title: Picking on the Same Person: Does Algorithmic Monoculture lead to Outcome Homogenization?

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the rate of 'systemic failure' where specific individuals are exclusively assigned negative outcomes across multiple independent decision-making models due to shared training data or foundation models.

Calculating group-level outcome homogenization metrics for 9 self-identified US Census racial categories using the ACS PUMS dataset to see if shared training data disproportionately systemically excludes certain racial groups.

Grouping text inputs from language datasets (IMDB, AGNews, Yahoo, HateSpeech18) based on the frequency of gendered pronouns/words (male vs. female) and measuring group-level outcome homogenization across models adapted from RoBERTa.

Measuring group-level outcome homogenization on computer vision models trained on the CelebA dataset, evaluating systemic failure rates across groups defined by physical attributes like hair color and the presence of a beard.
